acc_load_ctx_from_dlg.description: The function loads and exposes the accounting context of the currently in-use dialog.

acc_log_request.description: reports on a request, for example, it can be used to report on missed calls to off-line users who are replied 404 - Not Found.

acc_new_leg.description: Creates a new leg and increments [$acc_current_leg](#pv_acc_current_leg "1.7.3.$acc_current_leg (read-only)") only if multi-leg accounting is used.

acc_unload_ctx_from_dlg.description: The function off-loads a previosuly loaded accounting context, exposing whatever accounting context was present before doing the load.

do_accounting.description: replaces all the *_flag and, *_missed_flag, cdr_flag, failed transaction_flag and the db_table_avp modparams.

drop_accounting.description: resets flags and types of accounting set with do_accounting().

sl_reply_error.description: Sends back an error reply describing the nature of the last internal error.

sl_send_reply.description: For the current request, a reply is sent back having the given code and text reason.

t_add_cancel_reason.description: This function is used to enforce from the script level a custom "Reason" header into a CANCEL request.

t_add_hdrs.description: Attach a set of headers to the existing transaction - these headers will be appended to all requests related to the transaction (outgoing branches, local ACKS, CANCELs).

t_anycast_replicate.description: This function is used in an anycast setup to replicate a _CANCEL_ or _ACK_ method for whom there are no local transactions found.

t_cancel_branch.description: This function is to be call when a reply is received for cancelling a set of branches (see flags) of the current call.

t_check_status.description: Returns true if the regualr expression “re” match the reply code of the response message as follows: * in routing block - the code of the last sent reply.

t_check_trans.description: Returns true if the current request is associated to a transaction.

t_flush_flags.description: Flush the flags from current request into the already created transaction.

t_get_branch_idx_by_attr.description: This function may be used to search for the index of another branch of the current transaction.

t_inject_branches.description: The function adds new SIP branches (destinations) to an existing transaction and fires them (sends them out).

t_local_replied.description: Returns true if all or last (depending of the parameter) reply(es) were local generated (and not received).

t_new_request.description: This function generates and sends out a new SIP request (in a stateful way).

t_newtran.description: Creates the SIP transaction for the currently processed SIP request, thus switching to stateful processing.

t_on_branch.description: Sets a branch route to be execute separately for each branch of the transaction before being sent out - changes in that route should reflect only on that branch.

t_on_failure.description: Sets reply routing block, to which control is passed after a transaction completed with a negative result but before sending a final reply.

t_on_reply.description: Sets reply routing block, to which control is passed each time a reply (provisional or final) for the transaction is received.

t_relay.description: Relay a message statefully to destination indicated in current URI.

t_replicate.description: Replicates a request to another destination.

t_reply.description: Sends a stateful SIP reply to the currently processed requests.

t_reply_by_callid.description: This function is used to send a reply to an existing INVITE transaction.

t_reply_with_body.description: Sends a stateful SIP reply with a body to the currently processed requests.

t_wait_for_new_branches.description: This function instructs the existing SIP transaction to wait for new branches to be injected even after the completion of the existing branches.

t_wait_no_more_branches.description: This function instructs the existing SIP transaction to stop wait for new any new branches to be injected.

t_was_cancelled.description: Retuns true if called for an INVITE transaction that was explicitly cancelled by UAC side via a CANCEL request.

t_write_req.description: Write via FIFO file or UNIX socket a lot of information regarding the request.

t_write_unix.description: Write via FIFO file or UNIX socket a lot of information regarding the request.

t_hash.description: Gets information about the load of TM internal hash table.

t_reply.description: Generates and sends a reply for an existing inbound SIP transaction.

t_uac_cancel.description: Generates and sends a CANCEL for an existing SIP request.

t_uac_dlg.description: Generates and sends a local SIP request.

$(acc_leg(tag_name)[leg_index]).description: This variable can be addressed with the tag names defined using leg_fields and a valid leg index (<= $acc_current_leg).

$TS.description: Reference to startup unix time stamp.

$T_branch_idx.description: the index (starting with 0 for the first branch) of the currently proccessed branch.

$T_branch_last_reply_code.description: returns the last reply code received for a branch specified as parameter.

$T_fr_inv_timeout.description: the timeout for the final reply to an INVITE request, after a 1XX reply was received.

$T_fr_timeout.description: the timeout for the final reply to the current transaction.

$T_id.description: returns the ID of the current transaction.

$T_reply_code.description: the code of the reply, as follows: in request_route will be the last stateful sent reply; in reply_route will be the current processed reply; in failure_route will be the negative winning reply.

$T_ruri.description: the ruri of the current branch; this information is taken from the transaction structure, so you can access this information for any sip message (request/reply) that has a transaction.

$Ts.description: Reference to current unix time stamp in seconds.

$Tsm.description: Reference to current microseconds of the current second.

$aU.description: Whole username from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$acc_current_leg.description: Holds the index of the current leg, starting from 0.

$acc_extra(tag_name).description: This variable can addresed with the tag names defined using extra_fields.

$ad.description: Domain part of username from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$adu.description: URI from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$ai.description: Reference to URI in request's P-Asserted-Identity header (see RFC 3325).

$an.description: The nonce from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$ar.description: Realm from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$argv.description: Provides access to command line arguments specified with '-o' option.

$au.description: User part of username from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$auth.alg.description: The algorithm string from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$auth.nc.description: The value of nonce count parameter from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$auth.nonce.description: The nonce string from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$auth.opaque.description: The opaque string from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$auth.qop.description: The value of qop parameter from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$auth.resp.description: The authentication response from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header.

$avp(name).description: Attribute Value Pairs are dynamic variables linked to a singular message or transaction.

$bavp(name).description: a particular type of avp that can have different values for each branch.

$bf.description: Displays a list with the branch flags set for the current SIP request.

$branch.description: This variable is used for creating new branches by writing into it the value of a SIP URI.

$branch.fields.description: Provides read/write access to all fields/attributes of an already existing branch.

$branch.flag.description: Provides read/write access to the value of a single certain branch flag (identified by name).

$cT.description: Reference to body of Content-Type header and also the content-type headers inside a multi-part body.

$cfg_file.description: Holds the current name of the cfg file being executed, useful when using multiple scripts via the include statement.

$cfg_line.description: Holds the current line from the script of the action being executed, useful for logging purposes.

$challenge.algorithm.description: The algorithm value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

$challenge.ck.description: The ck value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

$challenge.ik.description: The ik value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

$challenge.nonce.description: The nonce value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

$challenge.opaque.description: The opaque value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

$challenge.qop.description: The qop value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

$challenge.realm.description: The realm value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

$ci.description: Reference to body of call-id header.

$cl.description: Reference to body of content-length header.

$cs.description: Reference to cseq number from cseq header.

$ct.description: Reference to contact instance/body from the contact header.

$ct.fields.description: Reference to the fields of a contact instance/body.

$dP.description: Reference to transport protocol of destination uri.

$dd.description: Reference to domain of destination uri.

$dip.description: Reference to Diversion header 'privacy' parameter value.

$dir.description: Reference to Diversion header 'reason' parameter value.

$dp.description: Reference to port of destination uri.

$du.description: Reference to destination uri (outbound proxy to be used for sending the request).

$err.class.description: The class of error (now is '1' for parsing errors).

$fU.description: Reference to username in URI of 'From' header.

$fd.description: Reference to domain in URI of 'From' header.

$fn.description: Reference to display name of 'From' header.

$ft.description: Reference to tag parameter of 'From' header.

$hdr.description: Represents the body of the N-th header identified by 'name'.

$hdrcnt.description: Returns number of headers of type given by 'name'.

$log_level.description: Changes the log level for the current process; the log level can be set to a new value or it can be reset back to the global log level.

$mf.description: Displays a list with the message/transaction flags set for the current SIP request.

$msg.branch.description: Used for creating new message branches by writing into it the value of a SIP URI.

$msg.branch.attr.description: Similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating over a single branch attribute (attached to the current branch).

$msg.branch.duri.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with the Detination-URI value of the message branch.

$msg.branch.flag.description: Similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating over a single branch flag (for the current branch).

$msg.branch.flags.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with list (comma separated) of per-branch flags (which are set for the branch).

$msg.branch.last_idx.description: Returns the index of the last message branch.

$msg.branch.path.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with the PATH value of the message branch.

$msg.branch.q.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with the Q value of the message branch.

$msg.branch.socket.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with the (forced) socket value of the message branch.

$msg.branch.uri.description: Gives read / write access over the SIP URI (as string) of an existing message branch.

$msg.flag.description: Provides read/write access to the value of a single certain message flag (identified by name).

$msg.is_request.description: Tells if the current SIP message is a request or not.

$msg.type.description: Returns the type of the current message.

$oP.description: Reference to transport protocol of original R-URI.

$oU.description: Reference to username in request's original URI.

$od.description: Reference to domain in request's original R-URI.

$op.description: Reference to port of original R-URI.

$pU.description: Reference to user in request's P-Preferred-Identity header URI (see RFC 3325).

$param.description: Retrieves the parameters of the route.

$pd.description: Reference to domain in request's P-Preferred-Identity header URI (see RFC 3325).

$pn.description: Reference to Display Name in request's P-Preferred-Identity header (see RFC 3325).

$pu.description: Reference to URI in request's P-Preferred-Identity header (see RFC 3325).

$rP.description: Reference to transport protocol of R-URI.

$rU.description: Reference to username in request's URI.

$rb.description: Reference to the body or a body part of the SIP message.

$rc.description: Reference to returned code by last invoked function.

$rd.description: Reference to domain in request's URI.

$return.description: Returns the value of the previously executed route.

$route.description: Access route names of the current route call stack.

$route.name.description: Access the name of the current route.

$route.type.description: Access the type of the current route.

$rt.description: Reference to URI of refer-to header.

$ru_q.description: Reference to q value of the R-URI.

$sdp.description: Read/Write reference to the SDP body of the current SIP message.

$sdp.line.description: Read/Write reference to SDP body lines, with filtering support.

$sdp.session.description: Read/Write reference to the SDP body session, with filtering support.

$sdp.stream.description: Read/Write reference to SDP body streams, with filtering support.

$sdp.stream.idx.description: Read-Only reference to the index of the matched SDP stream.

$si.description: Reference to IP source address of the message.

$socket_in.description: Read-only variable to get the description (proto:ip:port format) of the inbound socket (used for receiving the message).

$socket_out.description: Read-write variable for reading or changing the outbound socket of the message.

$sp.description: Reference to the source port of the message.

$tU.description: Reference to username in URI of 'To' header.

$td.description: Reference to domain in URI of 'To' header.

$time.description: Returns the string formatted time according to UNIX date (see: man date).

$tm.branch.attr.description: similar to $tm.branch.uri, but gives read/write access to the attributed attached to the branch.

$tm.branch.duri.description: 100% similar to $tm.branch.uri, but returning the Detination-URI value of the branch.

$tm.branch.flag.description: similar to $tm.branch.uri, but gives read/write access to a single branch flag (by its name).

$tm.branch.flags.description: 100% similar to $tm.branch.uri, but returning the list (comma separated) of per-branch flags which are set for the branch.

$tm.branch.last_received.description: 100% similar to $tm.branch.uri, but returning the reply code of the last received reply (from the network) on this branch.

$tm.branch.path.description: 100% similar to $tm.branch.uri, but returning the PATH value of the branch.

$tm.branch.q.description: 100% similar to $tm.branch.uri, but returning the Q value of the branch.

$tm.branch.socket.description: 100% similar to $tm.branch.uri, but returning the socket description (proto:ip:port) used for sending the branch out.

$tm.branch.type.description: 100% similar to $tm.branch.uri, but returning the type of the current branch.

$tm.branch.uri.description: gives read-only access over the Request URI (as string) of a TM existing branch.

$tn.description: Reference to display name of 'To' header.

$tt.description: Reference to tag parameter of 'To' header.

$ua.description: Reference to user agent header field.

$var(name).description: Script variables are strictly bound to the script routes.

$xlog_level.description: Allows to set /reset the xlog() logging level on per-process bases.
